function: Estimates the time-varying frequency-selective uplink MIMO-OFDM channel: block-wise planar LMMSE estimate, then a 3D dilated residual CNN refines and interpolates it over pilot and data symbols (p. 3-4).
system: Uplink multiuser MIMO-OFDM: BS with 64 antennas, 24 single-antenna users, 48 subcarriers at 30 kHz spacing, 28 OFDM symbols (8 pilots); carrier band not stated; no RIS (p. 4).
method: LBPCE: LMMSE estimate of a block-wise planar channel model, then a 3D dilated residual CNN (3D-DRCN) trained offline in a supervised way with L1 loss and Adam (p. 3-4).
data_channel: CDL-B channel model of 3GPP TR 38.901 [16], simulated, for both training and testing; number of training samples not stated (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training: delay spread 100-300 ns, 80-120 km/h, SNR 4-14 dB. Testing: 129 ns, 100 km/h, SNR 4-18 dB; delay spread and speed inside the training ranges (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, 1D LMMSE, 2x1D LMMSE. Learned: CE-DNN, CE-CNN, SF-CNN, Model2, ICINet, LDAMP, LTMP, 2DU, 3DFF. Module A is an ablation. NMSE and complexity compared (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE in dB versus SNR; number of complex multiplications versus number of users (p. 5).
complexity: Complex multiplications: module A (NTp/VU)^3+6K(NTp/VU)^2+3KUVM(NTp/VU), module B (12170+30T)TpNMK/4; compared with baselines versus users in Fig. 5b (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "For the network training, we use the CDL-B channel model [16]". Ref. [16] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 5); the same CDL-B model is used for testing.
q2_support: p. 4: "For testing, we use the CDL-B channel with 129 ns r.m.s. delay spread and mobile speed of 100 km/h in the SNR range of 4-18 dB". Delay spread and speed lie inside the training ranges; only the SNR range extends, which does not count.
q3_support: p. 4: "LBPCE significantly outperforms the CE-DNN, CE-CNN, SF-CNN, Model2, ICINet, 2DU, 3DFF, LS". Learned networks plus LS and LMMSE (non-learned) are compared in NMSE, Fig. 5a.
q4_support: p. 4: "We use the number of complex multiplications to measure the computational complexity". The count of LBPCE is given on p. 4 and compared with the baselines in Fig. 5b (p. 5).
q5_support: p. 4: "For the network training, we use the CDL-B channel model [16]". Channels are simulated from a 3GPP model; the text gives no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2405.11218v1. Area 2: channel estimation, where the 3D-DRCN refines block-wise planar LMMSE estimates. Test delay spread (129 ns) and speed (100 km/h) lie inside the training ranges, and only the SNR range extends (4-18 dB versus 4-14 dB), so q2 = 0. Module A is an ablation of the proposed method, not counted as the baseline. Fig. 5b varies users for complexity only, not for NMSE. No code or data link found in the text.
